ares v148 has now been released.

This release includes big improvements to a number of ares cores. Highlights include rewrites to the N64 CPU & RSP JITs resulting in significant performance gains across the N64 library, additional implementation & accuracy improvements to the PlayStation core, fixes to the GBA core, and support for the Famicom data recorder & Dendy. 

Additionally, there have been many updates to the core ares application across all platforms. Per-core input configuration has been added, updated video, audio, & input drivers are available, bug fixes, additional options have been added, and core dependencies have been updated. 

Since v147, 20 contributors have created 300 commits to the ares codebase.

As always, if you wish to see the full changelog in a per-commit format along with their authors, you can do so on GitHub [here](https://github.com/ares-emulator/ares/compare/v147...v148).

releases.name: Cemu 2.6
releases.body:
**Changelog:**
- Exporting saves via the title manager no longer crashes when the export path contains unicode characters
- Fixed a regression in DS Virtual Console titles (#1440)
- Fixed a bug where the debug shader dumping option would try to write files to the wrong directory
- Added a right-click context menu to the PPC debugger disassembly view and fixed some smaller bugs in the debugger
- Use libusb as the backend for HID/USB devices on Windows (#1471)
- Reduce amount of Vulkan sampler objects that are created. Reduces memory usage slightly and avoids crashes on drivers that have a low limit on sampler objects
- Improved index data caching on Vulkan. This may provide a very small performance benefit in some games
- The `--force-interpreter` command line option now always uses single-threaded CPU emulation like originally intended

releases.name: Cemu 2.5
releases.body:
**Changelog:**
- Upscaling and downscaling options in the graphics settings now work correctly on Vulkan. Previously, the hermite and bicubic scaling options would only work on OpenGL and silently fall back to bilinear filtering on Vulkan
- Graphic pack support for custom scaling shaders has been reworked and is now functional on Vulkan, with fixes carrying over to OpenGL. If you are a graphic pack developer see #1392 for details
- Cemu will now show an error if the MLC directory is not writeable
- Added a workaround for graphic driver crashes seen in the eShop versions of Fatal Frame. These are caused by the game shipping with shaders that contain infinite loops. The actual hardware has an escape mechanism for this that we don't yet emulate
- Added support for connecting Wiimotes via L2CAP on Linux (Details in #1353)
- Set correct version for MacOS bundle
- Updated Arabic, German, Russian and Swedish translations

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.6
releases.body:
Sixth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android, and the first with **PS4 backward compatibility**: PS4 games now run in CapyPS5 the way they do on a real PS5. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New: PS4 backward compatibility**

A PS5 runs PS4 games on its own hardware. CapyPS5 does the same in software: PS4 games use the same x86-64 JIT, system libraries and Vulkan renderer as PS5 games, and only what the PS4 does differently was added.
- **GPU:** PS4 (GCN gfx7) shaders and registers, PS4 render targets and texture tiling, CMASK and HTile fast clears, cube and volume textures, and the PS4 Gnm driver calls.
- **System:** PS4 executables and the modules games ship, the PS4 memory layout and flexible memory budget, and PS4 save data and trophies.
- PS4 games go in the same game folders as PS5 games (a folder with `eboot.bin` and `sce_sys/param.sfo`) and carry a **PS4** mark in the library.
- This is the first release with it. 2D and Unity games run best; Unreal Engine 4 games start but are slow; many games don't boot yet. Lower the resolution for big games.

**Also new**

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.5
releases.body:
Fifth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Mali GPUs on their system driver can now run games, and the FPS counter shows how many frames CapyPS5 Framegen adds. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **Mali on the system driver:** that driver cannot sample BCn compressed textures, so the GPU used to be rejected. CapyPS5 now decompresses those textures on the GPU when it uploads them (BC1 to BC7, including BC6H HDR textures). GPUs that support BCn keep using it directly.
- **PanVK on Mali:** the GPU is no longer rejected when the driver lacks vertex-stage stores or dual-source blending.
- **Framegen counter:** with CapyPS5 Framegen on, the FPS counter reads *XX FPS - YY FG*: XX are the game's own frames, YY the total including generated ones. The options are now called *Framegen x2*, *x3* and *x4*.
- **HDR10 output:** games that output HDR10 are converted to SDR for the screen.

**Fixed**
- Tessellation: quad domains, fractional-even spacing, counterclockwise output and masked hull control points.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.4
releases.body:
Fourth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. More than 100 games now run correctly according to testers' reports, and this release adds CapyPS5 Framegen. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **CapyPS5 Framegen:** optional frame generation. It draws in-between frames from the motion between two game frames, so a game at 30 FPS is shown at 60. Off by default; turn it on in *Settings → Performance* (1 per frame, or up to 3). Adds one frame of latency and some GPU load; works best from 25 FPS up.
- New performance options in *Settings → Performance*: shadow resolution, early depth testing and a frame rate limit (30 or 20 FPS).
- Physical keyboard input and an on-screen keyboard toggle for text fields, and system dialogs that can now be answered.
- Android 16 and devices with 16 KB memory pages are supported.

**Fixed**
- Unreal Engine 5 games: graphics and async compute hand work back and forth several times per frame, and each hand-off waited up to 100 ms. Menus that ran at 0–2 FPS now move.
- Games whose shadows use depth-compare texture gathers (Castlevania: Belmont's Curse) closed after the menu.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.3
releases.body:
Third alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Fixes for the logs testers sent on v0.0.2, CPU work for Unreal Engine games, and more from KytyPS5. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Fixed**
- Games that use fibers (sceFiber) closed the emulator at start on ARM ("Fiber context switching is only implemented on x86_64", Toy Story Retro Roundup). Fibers now switch the game's own registers. First support: please report how fiber games behave.
- Final Fantasy VII Rebirth: sceKernelFtruncate, which it calls when saving, is now available.
- Mewgenics: pthread_setcanceltype is now available.
- The game clock (RDTSC) ran about 23 % faster than the frequency games are told; they now match.
- Very large GPU compute dispatches (over 65535 groups, as in Astro Bot) are split to fit Adreno limits.
- Unity backtraces no longer follow a bogus frame at the start of each guest thread.

**New**
- Unreal Engine games: the TLS and process clock reads they make millions of times a second run inside the game code instead of calling into the emulator.
- Shaders can read the real GPU clock (S_MEMREALTIME) on drivers that offer it.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.2 (Alpha)
releases.body:
Second alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Fixes for what testers reported on v0.0.1, a trophy screen, and 60 games on the compatibility list. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Fixed**
- Virtual controller: several buttons can now be held at once.
- Physical controllers: the left stick no longer presses the d-pad (it moved menus and cursors, as in Mewgenics).
- Adreno 6xx with Turnip (such as Adreno 660) no longer closes at start for lack of 8-bit storage (thanks to deivid22srk).
- Dead Cells has its music, hits and footsteps back: NGS2 voices sent to a rack handle are now heard.
- Games that use user clip planes or uncommon storage texture settings no longer close.

**New**
- Trophies: each game's trophy list, what you have earned, and a card to share your progress.
- A "What's new" card after each update.
- Over 35 improvements from KytyPS5: shaders, tessellation, NGS2 and ATRAC9 audio, flip waits and fewer crashes.

**2026-11-14 · Windows x64 · Linux x86_64 · macOS Intel**

- 支持 Vulkan 1.4+ API

releases.name: recomp-launcher 0.3.0
releases.body:
### Added
- The installer shows its version (the game's tag, or the short commit for a
  build off a branch) in the window's corner and title, and on start asks
  GitHub for the game's newest release: a newer one gets a download button.
  Offline it says nothing.
- `game.files` takes globs: `*.iso` makes a folder holding a disc image the
  game, for a title whose setup takes an image rather than an install.
- `installer.yml` takes `platforms` (default `windows linux macos`), so a
  Windows-only game doesn't publish installers that can't build it.
- A `game.files` entry may be alternatives, `a|b`: `HOVER.EXE|hover*.zip` is
  the game's folder or a folder holding a zip of it.

- The Windows installer carries version info and a manifest, and a release
  has `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so antivirus heuristics and players can check it.
- A log of why the installer stopped (`%APPDATA%\recomp-launcher\launcher.log`
  on Windows), and an error box instead of the window vanishing.

### Fixed
- On Windows a step line after a blank line was glued to the line before it
  (ConPTY skips the blank line with a cursor move), so the bar missed that step.

## SkyNetEmu 0.2.2

Source revision: `48f360d1edca3859f72e447e6943a21ee8eede91` (version code 5, version name `0.2.2-stable+48f360d`).

### Fixes and improvements

**Same game presets on every phone**
- Game presets are no longer limited to particular processors, and the Snapdragon-specific BeamNG Box64 presets are gone. Every phone sees the same presets.
- Presets no longer name a GPU driver; the app picks one for your GPU:
  - Linux games get a Turnip driver when a preset is imported, when a shortcut is created and when a game starts. Adreno 735, 740 and 750 get Mesa Turnip 26.2.2; Adreno 730 gets Turnip v27.0.0 r6; Adreno 8xx keeps its current driver.
  - Windows games get the driver mapped to your GPU when they start, or the system driver when none is mapped.

**Crashes**
- Games no longer crash with SIGSYS on Android versions whose system-call filter refuses calls FEX makes (all FEX + bionic BeamNG starts on a POCO F6 with Android 14 died this way). A refused call now fails normally and is logged to `Winlator/logs/sigsys.log`.

## SkyNetEmu 0.2.1

Source revision: `e750c469bed4a87644a1dac43ff7e1a137d32120` (version code 4, version name `0.2.1-stable+e750c46`).

### Fixes and improvements

**Counter-Strike 2**
- CS2 starts again on a fresh install. The game stopped with "A game file appears to be missing or corrupted" because its Panorama text library could not load next to the root filesystem's newer HarfBuzz. The app now carries the six small font libraries it needs (unmodified Debian 11 builds of HarfBuzz, FriBidi, libthai, libdatrie, Graphite2 and Pixman) instead of relying on Valve's Steam Linux Runtime 3.0 (sniper) being installed.
- The menu's background videos play from a Steam library on shared storage. The x86-64 and 32-bit x86 shims were missing the `flock` fallback that the aarch64 one already had, so file locks failed on shared storage.

**BeamNG.drive**
- BeamNG 0.39 and 0.40 now offer a single preset: FEX + bionic, no PRoot, direct launch, 960x544. The Box64, Box64 bionic, SoC-specific Box64 and Windows ARM64 presets are removed from those two versions; older BeamNG versions keep theirs.

- **Frame generation is smooth again when the game runs below half the screen's refresh rate.** The FPS counter used to double, but each generated frame and the real one reached the screen on back-to-back refreshes (about 8 ms apart, then a 25 ms gap), so motion looked no smoother than without frame generation. This was reported on a OnePlus 11 with BeamNG 0.34. Now the frames are shown evenly spaced, for example every 16.7 ms when 30 FPS is doubled to 60 on a 120 Hz screen. Checked for Linux games on Box64 + bionic and FEX + bionic. Windows games with frame generation go through the same code, but were not tested.
- Frame generation now caps the game's own frame rate at the screen's refresh rate divided by the multiplier (60 for 2x on a 120 Hz screen), since the extra frames could not be shown anyway.

Game profiles and the other registry files are read from the tag `v0.2.4` of the components repository (the same content as `v0.2.3`).

**New**
- Upscaling to your screen resolution now uses AMD FSR 1 instead of GSR: a cleaner, sharper picture (#44). With sharpening on, it sharpens after upscaling, at the screen resolution.
- Experimental: SGSR 2, a temporal upscaler. It builds the picture from several frames at your screen resolution, for finer detail on edges and distant objects. Two options: at the normal 3D resolution, or at 75 % 3D resolution for more FPS.
- The gear (⚙) has one choice "Upscale to screen resolution": Off / FSR 1 / SGSR 2 / SGSR 2 at 3D 75 %. If you had the old upscale box on, you get FSR 1.

releases.name: PvZ: Replanted Android v0.1.4-beta
releases.body:
Fifth beta of the Android port of the PS5 version of **Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted** (AnyPS5 + Box64 + Turnip). Installs over earlier betas, game data and settings are kept.

> ⚠️ The game is not included — you need your own legally obtained, **decrypted** PS5 dump (PPSA29802).

### Fixes
- **A second player (2P) joined when pausing.** The game opens a second ("special") pad port, and it got the same input as the real pad, so Options there counted as player 2 joining. Only the standard port is the pad now.
- **Touches beside the on-screen buttons acted as a mouse**, a second input device for the game. The touch controls are the only player-1 input now (a real mouse or keyboard still works once used).

### Performance and heat
- **Built-in Turnip updated to Mesa 26.3** with our patch for importing the game's memory directly (no per-draw copies). If you picked another driver in *Settings → GPU driver*, switch back to **Built-in**: drivers without this import copy memory on every draw.

releases.name: PvZ: Replanted Android v0.1.3-beta
releases.body:
Fourth beta of the Android port of the PS5 version of **Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted** (AnyPS5 + Box64 + Turnip). Installs over earlier betas, game data and settings are kept.

> ⚠️ The game is not included — you need your own legally obtained, **decrypted** PS5 dump (PPSA29802).

### Fixes
- **Missing graphics and crashes on scene changes** (starting a level, the money bag at the end of a level): results the GPU writes back into game memory were silently skipped on pages the driver's write tracking had protected, so the game read stale or zero data. Menu elements that never showed up before (e.g. the Co-op / Vs. tombstone) are back.
- "storage texture has no committed guest pages" crash.

### Performance and heat
- Draw recipes now work for the menu (repeated draws reuse their recorded setup).
- Box64 spin-waits sleep (`PAUSE=3`, WFE) instead of spinning: less CPU load for the same frame rate.
- The driver's two threads wake each other only when one actually waits.

### Requirements
- Adreno (Snapdragon) GPU only; Android 11+ recommended. Tested on Snapdragon 8 Elite.

releases.body:
First public beta of the Android port of the PS5 version of **Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted**.

> ⚠️ The game is not included in the APK — you need your own **decrypted** PS5 dump (PPSA29802, the folder with `eboot.bin`).

- Android 8.0+, arm64.

- FPS limit 60/45/30 and "GPU turbo" in the launcher.

### Known issues
- Strong heating during long sessions → the phone lowers its clocks and FPS drops. For long sessions use the **45 FPS** limit.
- The menu is slower than levels (the driver is still single-threaded).
- A rare crash while a level loads — just restart.

releases.name: Galar Native v0.94
releases.body:
## Galar Native v0.94

### A steadier 30 fps with Graphics on Auto (#289 #300)
With Graphics on Auto, the game now starts at 85 % of its full 3D resolution (about 900p) and settles from there:
- It holds 30 for a calm minute: it goes up to the full resolution.
- It falls short of 30: it goes down to 720p.
- The phone gets hot: it goes down to 720p, and no lower for heat alone. Only a frame rate under 30 goes lower.

Before, the game started at full resolution and slower phones spent minutes under 30 before it stepped down. Under 30 the game also runs slower than normal, which looks like slow motion. If you picked a 3D render scale by hand in the menu, your choice is kept and Auto doesn't change it.

**Slow motion with the 60 fps option (#299):** if your phone can't reach 60, set Frame rate to 30. With 60 selected on a phone that runs at 20, the game plays at a third of its speed.

### Fewer missing objects while new shaders build

releases.name: Galar Native v0.93
releases.body:
## Galar Native v0.93

### Fixed: crashes on game threads with tiny stacks
Some of the game's threads have very small stacks (16 KB). Our handling of the game's system calls ran on those stacks, and on some phones (when Android was tracing) it ran past their end and crashed. That handling now runs on a stack of its own. The same fix is in Arceus Native v0.42, where a player hit this crash twice.

### Fixed: a "device lost" now counts as a crash (#280)
When the graphics driver gave up ("device lost", seen on a Mali-G68), the game closed but the next start didn't know it had crashed. So the automatic safe start, which turns off risky features step by step on Arm's Mali driver, never stepped in. Now it does.

### No setup needed
Same shader translation as v0.87–v0.92: install and press Play.

Tested on a Galaxy S25+: field, walking and menus, no crash, locked 30 fps.

### Install
Install **GalarNative-v0.93.apk** over your current version. versionCode 93.

releases.name: Galar Native v0.91
releases.body:
## Galar Native v0.91

### Faster shader setup (#262)
Most of setup's shader time wasn't the translation, it was files. Setup kept its working files in `Android/data/…/files/setup_work`, where Android passes every file through a slow storage layer: on a Galaxy S25+, 10,000 small files took 26 s to write there and 0.5 s in the app's private storage. Setup writes about 130,000 of them.

- The shader steps' working files now go in the app's private storage. It's the same storage chip, so setup needs no more free space than before. `setup.log` and the unpacked game stay where they were.
- Packing the shaders compresses on every core at a faster setting, with the same result: 194 s → 7 s on a PC.

This applies to a full setup and to the automatic shader update. On a PC limited to 8 cores, translating all 38,501 shaders now takes about 9 minutes and packing about 15 seconds. These changes were tested on a PC; phone timings will follow.

### No setup needed
Same shader translation and engine as v0.88 to v0.90: install and press Play.

### Install
Install **GalarNative-v0.91.apk** over your current version. versionCode 91.
